That being said, $SOI accelerating from $25m quarterly photonics-SOI revenue… with no forward visibility earlier this year.

Into securing $1.2B in agreements this quarter, backed by cash, is extremely transformative and make me happy to see.

In terms transcript details:

- “AI data center have built large compute power, but some of it remains idle as copper links limit data availability for processing. 

Optics removes that bottleneck”

Reiterating what I said about aggregate capex not applying 1:1 with optical sector, given optical shifts improves GPU utilization

- timelines: “Near-package optics brings first volume by the end of the fiscal year, and high volume next year. 

Co-Packaged Optics for scale out is starting to ramp. TPO for scale up will be the next stage”

- “Growth comes in waves, scale out and scale up as a new driver. As those links goes optical, they create new volume on top of today's. 

In fiscal year 2027, our revenue comes mostly from pluggable transceiver, and we see initial volume from NPO.”

- “Growth returned sooner than we had anticipated and with more vigor. Revenue grew 39%, with Photonics-SOI leading the way.

Margin expansion has come forward too”

- “So, for the capacity reservation agreement we signed, they cover calendar year 2027, calendar year 2028, and beyond”

In terms of where they see acceleration:

- “Now we see and we believe the new requests that we are getting lately are more for the Co-Packaged Optics and NPO. And especially for the scale-up going forward.”

I think that this quarter earnings marks the inflection of optical acceleration for Soitec + silicon photonics.

And what it means for a chokepoint to transform into company economics.

BTC still has a very long way to go in its attempt to offer a credible alternative to a 5000 year old coveted shiny rock.

BTC succeeding and continuing to rise in value is good for all alt digital SOVs.

I really enjoyed Elon Musk’s interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin. While I always appreciate Elon’s candor, I don’t understand his long-term goal of interstellar travel. $SPCX should focus on achievable and economically viable goals like orbital space stations or outposts on the Moon.

The distance between stars is too vast, and the speeds at which we can realistically travel, especially given the fuel constraints of chemical rockets, are much too slow to make interstellar travel for biological humans feasible.

Plus, it’s not just humans who are constrained by the laws of physics, geometry, spacetime, and the reality of the universe. It’s highly unlikely that there are any other spacefaring civilizations, no matter how advanced their propulsion systems, that are capable of interstellar travel either.

Like @elonmusk, I’m also a Star Trek fan. It would be great if there really were a way to travel faster than light at warp speed through subspace, circumventing the insurmountable obstacles of speed, fuel, mass, distance, the interstellar medium, and time dilation that combine to make interstellar travel through actual spacetime realistically impossible.

When it comes to interstellar travel or a federation of planets, science fiction really is fiction. Elon should focus his genius on the aspects of science fiction that are scientifically possible.

India is the only place I've felt genuine 'culture shock'. I spent a good few months there when I was younger, with little money, and this was my experience

The first word I think of, when I think of India is overwhelming. In almost every sense:

- The diversity and flavour of the food
- The celebration and visibility of religion and spirituality
- The importance of, and passion for, cricket
- The density of people, noise and traffic
- The scale and proximity of inequality
- The intensity of social interaction, from negotiating everything to the directness of personal questions
- The warm and welcoming nature of the people and their desire to share their culture, both nationally and locally
- The chaotic nature of everyday life, where everything feels co-ordinated in its own disorganisation

Overall, I think India is best understood through its contradictions, both in individual places and across states. One of the biggest of these is how incredibly warm people are individually, and yet how impersonal things can feel in the aggregate, where bureaucratic systems are a nightmare and corruption is commonplace

I remember waiting for a bus and asking a guy at the bus stop when it would arrive. 'Soon, don't worry' A couple of hours passed, so I asked again. 'Soon, my friend' Eventually it got dark, and I asked him one final time. 'Ah, it comes tomorrow. Let's go eat something, macha?'

It's that sort of thing that takes a while to adjust to. Indians seem to have an insanely high tolerance for chaos, and you've got to learn to rely on adjust karna. The idea that you will simply accommodate delays and changes as they happen

It's the type of place you're so happy you've been to, but have a sense of relief when you leave

I imagine that as a tourist with money, you'll experience many of the same things but remain more insulated from them, becoming more of an observer. If you go, go see the beauty of the country but also try to talk to people and experience some of everyday life. The people and communities is what makes India so distinctive

One day I'll probably go back and see it more from this POV. For now it remains a country I have a lot of love for, even if that love is complicated

I never looked at the X algorithm before today. It's open source, and they have a file called param .rs with the actual weights used to rank your “For You feed”

The most surprising thing: copying a post's link has a weight of 20. Liking it has a weight of 0.7. Copying the link is the most valuable thing you can do with a post, weighted almost 30x more than a like and 4x more than a reply.

My guess why: when you copy a link, you're about to paste it somewhere else. A group chat, Slack, an email. That's the strongest signal there is that a post is worth something, and it brings new people onto X. A like costs nothing. Sending something to a friend means you're putting your name on it.

The rest of the list tells a bit of a similar story like a reply is 5, a quote is 5, sharing by DM is 5, following the author is 4, a share is 2.1, a repost is 1, and a like is 0.7. Literally I didn’t know that repost does almost nothing. 

The negatives are brutal btw a report is -234, a mute is -59, "not interested" is -53 and a block is -31.

A reply from someone you follow who follows you back gets a 15x boost. Conversations between real connections matter most (and not bots!)

Reposts don't reach strangers. A filter drops a repost for anyone who doesn't follow the reposter. A quote is a new post, so it can travel much further. Quote beats repost so you always have to add your own thoughts to a post. 

Your post leaves For You after 48 hours. Small accounts get guaranteed test slots while a post is under 2 hours old with fewer than 200 views, so the first 2 hours decide a lot.

Interestingly hashtags aren't read anywhere in the ranking code. They are not a thing anymore. Your text and images are turned into vectors and matched to people with similar interests.

So if you want a post to spread, write something people want to send to one specific person. Likes are nice, but they barely move anything.

thread_tweets.text: Racks ship dry and are filled in the hall. A dry GB300 fits the standard 1,500kg freight lift and a filled one does not, so the lift sees the dry rack and the floor carries the filled one. Raising an upper floor’s rating means strengthening slabs, beams, columns and foundations, often in post-tensioned concrete that cannot be cut. Coolant pipes and busway hung above the racks add more load. New AI capacity goes into single story halls or buildings designed for the weight from the start. (3/3)

thread_tweets.text: The coolant alone, a mix of water and propylene glycol, adds roughly 500 to 1,000lb. Most datacenter floors were built for the 2011 rack. The industry standard (TIA-942) asks for 150 to 250lb per square foot, or 7 to 12kPa. A GB300 rack puts about 17kPa on its own footprint dry and 22kPa filled. Multistory sites in Singapore are rated 5 to 15kPa per floor. (2/3)
